target_customer: Hedge funds, private equity and infrastructure investors, consultants and equipment makers buying data center supply chain research
problem: Investors lack granular, early data on data center buildout bottlenecks such as generators, power equipment, memory and project delays. Meteor Labs extracts it from public filings with browser agents.
business_model: Subscription research and data product sold to investors
product_category: Alternative data, data center supply chain intelligence

founders.name: Pranav Madhukar
education: University of Washington, computer science (left to build the company)
founders.background_notes: YC page mentions NSF funded math at UChicago and browser agent research.

founders.name: Farhan Khan
education: University of Washington (left to build the company)
founders.background_notes: YC page gives only the first name Farhan; GeekWire and launch coverage give Khan.

competitors.name: Perplexity Comet
competitors.what: Chromium based browser with built in AI assistant and agents (relevant to the original Meteor browser idea)

competitors.name: The Browser Company Dia
competitors.what: AI native browser successor to Arc, beta from June 2025

technical_complexity.rationale: Original idea was forking Chromium into an agentic browser (hard). The current research product uses browser agents to scrape esoteric public filings and needs domain analysis, a moderate engineering load.

defensibility.rationale: Curated project and equipment datasets could accumulate, but sources are public records and larger alt data vendors can replicate.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: For the browser idea, well funded AI browsers were already shipping in 2025. The company later moved to a different market; no acquisition found.

market_need_then: In 2025 the AI browser category was heating up, and later AI data center buildout drove investor demand for supply chain data. The company's site cites coverage of 500 plus US data center projects (self reported).

branding.domain_note: Uses meteorlabs.ai while the earlier browser lived at browse.dev

identity.visual_style: Research publication style site with dated research notes
identity.voice_and_tone: Analytical research notes, for example Slots Beat Specs

rebrands.to: Meteor Labs (data center supply chain research)
rebrands.why: Not stated in sources; exact date unknown

branding.community_and_virality: Browser launch got GeekWire coverage as UW students joining YC to take on Chrome

brand_strength.rationale: Name shared with Meteor Development Group and other Meteors. Early GeekWire coverage was about the browser, not the current research brand.

pivots.from: Meteor, an agentic AI browser forked from Chromium (alpha, launched 2025-08)
pivots.to: Data center supply chain intelligence for hedge funds
pivots.why: Not stated in sources. Date unknown: between September 2025 (browser interview) and October 2026 (research notes on the site).

outcome_analysis: Meteor Labs is active with two founders. The YC Summer 2025 launch was an agentic browser covered by GeekWire, and the company now sells data center supply chain research to investors with notes published in October 2026. No funding round or revenue was verified, so no outcome verdict is possible, and the pivot reason and date are not public.
notes: YC page says founders raised 100K to 150K from university funding (figures conflict between profile and launch post); these are not venture rounds. Dealroom's 125K seed and VCBacked's 500K are aggregator claims, possibly about the browser entity, and are unverified. Competitors listed relate to the original browser idea at the 2025 batch; no dated competitor for the current data center research wedge was found.
